description: Pay your tuition from abroad without overpaying on fees or missing the deadline.

steps.detail: Your offer letter, the university's invoice, or the student portal shows the exact amount, currency, due date, and the university's bank details (account name, number, SWIFT/BIC, reference).
steps.title: Find the official payment instructions

steps.detail: Universities often list Flywire, Convera, or a direct bank transfer. Compare them with the assistant's transfer comparison — a 2% FX margin on $10,000 is $200.
steps.title: Compare the payment channels

steps.detail: Most schools require your student ID or invoice number in the payment reference. Without it, your money can sit unmatched for weeks.
steps.title: Prepare your student reference number

steps.detail: Initiate the transfer at least 5 business days before the due date. International wires can take 1-3 days; invoice platforms confirm in hours.
steps.title: Send the payment early

steps.detail: Save the receipt / transaction ID and upload it to the student portal if the university asks for proof of payment.
steps.title: Keep the receipt

steps.detail: Check the portal 3-5 days later to confirm the payment is matched to your account. If not, contact the finance office with your receipt.
steps.title: Confirm it arrived

tips: Never pay tuition through a 'discount agent' offering a better rate on social media — it's the most common student scam.
If the amount is large, ask your bank about the reporting threshold in your country first.
title: How to pay tuition from abroad
